observations: Retried read-only public recovery of the PLOS/Figshare S1 Code artifact identified by the prior role-local checkpoint; public search did not expose the future-dated item and the plos.figshare.com root returned HTTP 403 in the available public transport.
No source file from S1 Code was obtained in this invocation, so no source-exact S8/S11/S12 reproduction or code-semantics claim was made.
public_source_recovery.scope: Transport/reproducibility observation only; no negative claim about artifact existence or paper validity.

bounded_audit.status: calibrated local release detector for dormant-memory stability-plasticity tradeoff; non-reproduction

design.purpose: Replace the prior hand-set release threshold with a separately calibrated causal detector using only already-observed prequential error, then test delayed/sparse feedback and tracker dependence.
design.stream: synthetic linear latent stream, ambient N=32, latent dimension 5, tracked rank k=4, trajectory length 700; task event time randomized uniformly in a 101-step window.
design.temporary_silence: two independent task-relevant latent modes are strongly attenuated over overlapping unknown windows in the no-switch condition; the target continues to depend on them.
design.true_switch: a task-relevant old mode becomes weak and a previously secondary fifth mode becomes task-relevant at a randomized event time; a separate earlier temporary silence is included as nuisance evidence.

trackers.oja_like: source-closer bounded Oja-like orthonormal update; not source-exact SPLiT

design.memory_proxy: A slow subspace tracker serves as dormant-memory/stability path and a ten-times-faster tracker as flexible/plastic path; both use matched intrinsic normalized-LMS decoders.
design.detector: One-sided decayed CUSUM over observed prequential squared-loss advantage slow-minus-fast. Threshold h and required positive-evidence persistence are selected only on disjoint calibration seeds; runtime decisions use no future labels.
design.calibration: For each tracker and feedback condition, 6 temporary-silence plus 6 true-switch calibration streams. Grid h={1,2,4,8,12,16,24}, persistence={1,3,5,8}; objective is post-event hybrid MSE plus a fixed false-release penalty.
design.heldout: For each tracker and feedback condition, 12 temporary-silence plus 12 true-switch streams on disjoint seeds. Bootstrap intervals use held-out paired stream differences.

interpretation: A detector calibrated on disjoint seeds can convert local prequential error into a useful release signal in this bounded stability-plasticity setting without consulting future labels.

The result is not tracker-invariant: PAST/GROUSE-like tracking retained significant switch benefit even with 20-step delayed, 50%-sparse error, while the bounded Oja-like tracker lost measurable benefit and released much later under the same feedback restriction.

There is no universal threshold: independently calibrated h/persistence differ materially between PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like dynamics. Any biologically/local release mechanism must therefore be calibrated to tracker timescale and feedback availability rather than treated as a generic add-on.
Delayed/sparse feedback primarily raises release latency; for the Oja-like path it becomes a dominant bottleneck in this audit.
limits: Synthetic linear latent stream; no nonlinear manifold or source-exact recurrent SPLiT dynamics.

The slow-versus-fast parallel trackers are an engineering proxy for dormant subspace memory and release, not the exact decoder-anchored memory mechanism from the prior audit and not an established biological mechanism.
The detector runs two candidate trackers in parallel, so it is not yet the minimal O(Nk) single-state implementation sought for a biological/local mechanism.
Calibration sets are small and condition-specific; intervals are over 12 held-out streams per scenario, so effect-size precision remains limited.
Base learning still uses the same delayed/sparse label stream; the audit does not address fully unsupervised task-change detection.

candidate_update.positive_scope: In bounded held-out streams, separately calibrated prequential CUSUM released a stable/dormant path after true task-relevant subspace change and reduced post-switch error for PAST/GROUSE-like tracking under both full and delayed/sparse feedback, and for Oja-like tracking under full feedback.
candidate_update.negative_boundary: The same detector family was not robustly beneficial for the Oja-like tracker under 20-step delayed, 50%-sparse error; false releases remained 4/12 and median release latency reached 179 steps. No tracker-invariant or Oja-specific advantage is established.

bounded_audit.exact_next_action: Retry read-only S1 Code recovery. If still blocked, replace the parallel slow/fast proxy with a single O(Nk) dormant-memory tracker plus a calibrated local change statistic. Test nonlinear manifolds, multiple stochastic task switches, multiple disappearing/reappearing modes, and more severe delayed/sparse error. Calibrate on disjoint streams and report held-out false-release, release-latency and task-loss Pareto curves. Compare matched-budget PAST/GROUSE-like and source-closer Oja variants; explicitly test whether tracker-timescale normalization can make detector thresholds transferable. Keep conclusions bounded until source-exact S8/S11/S12 code is recovered.
